--- title: Detecting invasive mammals for management in Patagonia subtitle: Obtaining nature media with the R package suwo author: Marcelo Araya-Salas, PhD date: "2026-10-02" toc: true toc-depth: 3 toc-location: left number-sections: true highlight-style: pygments format: html: df-print: kable code-fold: true code-tools: true css: qmd.css editor_options: chunk_output_type: console --- ::: {.cell} ::: Source code and data found at [https://github.com/maRce10/suwo_publication](https://github.com/maRce10/suwo_publication) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # options to customize chunk outputs knitr::opts_chunk$set( tidy.opts = list(width.cutoff = 65), tidy = TRUE, message = FALSE ) ``` ::: ::: {.alert .alert-warning} This analysis serves as the invasive-species-management case study accompanying the manuscript **"Obtaining nature media with the R package suwo"**, illustrating how suwo-retrieved images can be carried into a model-training pipeline. ::: ::: {.alert .alert-info} # Purpose {.unnumbered .unlisted} - Assemble images of the focal management species -- American Mink (*Neogale vison*), Black Rat (*Rattus rattus*), and *Lontra* otters (*L. provocax*, *L. annectens*, *L. longicaudis*, *L. canadensis*, *L. felina*) -- from iNaturalist using the R package `suwo`. - Test whether pretrained YOLO models (trained on COCO classes) already detect the focal individuals well enough to bootstrap training labels. - Auto-generate YOLO-format training labels from those pretrained-model detections, remapped to the focal classes. - Train and evaluate a YOLO model to detect and classify the focal species, for use in an automated trap-release system targeting the invasive American Mink in Patagonia. ::: # Analysis flowchart {.unnumbered .unlisted} ```{mermaid} flowchart LR A[Query & download images] --> B(Preview pretrained-model detections) B --> C(Auto-generate labels) C --> D(Train / validation split) D --> E(Train YOLO model) E --> F(Evaluate) style A fill:#382A5433 style B fill:#395D9C33 style C fill:#3497A933 style D fill:#60CEAC33 style E fill:#60CEAC33 style F fill:#60CEAC33 ``` # Load packages {.unnumbered .unlisted} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # if sketchy not installed install it if (!require("sketchy")) { install.packages("sketchy") } # install/ load packages sketchy::load_packages(packages = c("knitr", "tidyverse", "ggpattern", github = "maRce10/suwo", "reticulate")) ``` ::: ::: {.alert .alert-info} The model-training steps below are Python (`ultralytics`, `opencv-python`), run through `reticulate`. They assume a Python environment with those packages already installed (e.g. `pip install ultralytics opencv-python`) and, for training, a CUDA-capable GPU. ::: ::: {.alert .alert-info} Raw images are **not** included in this repository (tens of thousands of files, downloaded on demand). Query metadata, auto-generated labels, and the train/validation split are also not included -- they are reproducible from the chunks below, which default to `eval: false` since every step here is either a slow bulk download or requires a GPU. The one artifact kept for reference is the log of an actual download run: [`data/raw/mink_detection_logs/download_images.log`](../data/raw/mink_detection_logs/download_images.log) (1,131 of 1,461 files downloaded successfully in that run, ~3.9 hours). ::: # Query and download images ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Folder layout, relative to the project root IMAGES_FOLDER <- "./data/raw/mink_detection_images" QUERIES_FOLDER <- "./data/processed/mink_detection_queries" dir.create(IMAGES_FOLDER, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE) dir.create(QUERIES_FOLDER, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE) # ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Queries ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ American Mink neogale_vison <- query_inaturalist(species = "Neogale vison", format = "image") # ~12 minutes write.csv(neogale_vison, paste0(QUERIES_FOLDER, "/neogale_vison.csv"), row.names = FALSE) # Rat rattus_rattus <- query_inaturalist(species = "Rattus rattus", format = "image") # ~25 minutes write.csv(rattus_rattus, paste0(QUERIES_FOLDER, "/rattus_rattus.csv"), row.names = FALSE) # Lontras: L. provocax, L. annectens, L. longicaudis, L. # canadensis, L. felina lontra_provocax <- query_inaturalist(species = "Lontra provocax", format = "image") write.csv(lontra_provocax, paste0(QUERIES_FOLDER, "/lontra_provocax.csv"), row.names = FALSE) lontra_annectens <- query_inaturalist(species = "Lontra annectens", format = "image") write.csv(lontra_annectens, paste0(QUERIES_FOLDER, "/lontra_annectens.csv"), row.names = FALSE) lontra_longicaudis <- query_inaturalist(species = "Lontra longicaudis", format = "image") write.csv(lontra_longicaudis, paste0(QUERIES_FOLDER, "/lontra_longicaudis.csv"), row.names = FALSE) lontra_canadensis <- query_inaturalist(species = "Lontra canadensis", format = "image") # ~17 minutes write.csv(lontra_canadensis, paste0(QUERIES_FOLDER, "/lontra_canadensis.csv"), row.names = FALSE) lontra_felina <- query_inaturalist(species = "Lontra felina", format = "image") write.csv(lontra_felina, paste0(QUERIES_FOLDER, "/lontra_felina.csv"), row.names = FALSE) # ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Download images ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ N_CORES <- 20 neogale_vison <- read.csv(paste0(QUERIES_FOLDER, "/neogale_vison.csv")) download_media(metadata = neogale_vison, cores = N_CORES, path = IMAGES_FOLDER) rattus_rattus <- read.csv(paste0(QUERIES_FOLDER, "/rattus_rattus.csv")) download_media(metadata = rattus_rattus, cores = N_CORES, path = IMAGES_FOLDER) lontra_provocax <- read.csv(paste0(QUERIES_FOLDER, "/lontra_provocax.csv")) download_media(metadata = lontra_provocax, cores = N_CORES, path = IMAGES_FOLDER) lontra_annectens <- read.csv(paste0(QUERIES_FOLDER, "/lontra_annectens.csv")) download_media(metadata = lontra_annectens, cores = N_CORES, path = IMAGES_FOLDER) lontra_longicaudis <- read.csv(paste0(QUERIES_FOLDER, "/lontra_longicaudis.csv")) download_media(metadata = lontra_longicaudis, cores = N_CORES, path = IMAGES_FOLDER) lontra_canadensis <- read.csv(paste0(QUERIES_FOLDER, "/lontra_canadensis.csv")) download_media(metadata = lontra_canadensis, cores = N_CORES, path = IMAGES_FOLDER) lontra_felina <- read.csv(paste0(QUERIES_FOLDER, "/lontra_felina.csv")) download_media(metadata = lontra_felina, cores = N_CORES, path = IMAGES_FOLDER) ``` ::: # Visualize data availability * Query metadata (saved above, one CSV per species) is combined to show how many images are available per species, and the same counts collapsed to `Lontra spp.` given how few images each individual otter species has relative to the mink and rat. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} queries_files <- list.files(path = "./data/processed/mink_detection_queries", pattern = "*.csv", full.names = TRUE) combined_data <- bind_rows(lapply(queries_files, read_csv)) combined_data %>% glimpse() # ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ # barplot of number of images per species combined_data %>% group_by(species) %>% summarise(n = n()) %>% ggplot(aes(x = species, y = n)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity") + theme_light() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) ggsave("./output/mink_detection_species_barplot.png", width = 1200, height = 800, scale = 1.2, units = "px") # ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ # same, but stack species with 'Lontra' in the name as 'Lontra # spp.' combined_data %>% mutate(species1 = ifelse(grepl("Lontra", species), "Lontra spp.", species)) %>% mutate(species = factor(species, levels = c("Neogale vison", "Rattus rattus", "Lontra provocax", "Lontra longicaudis", "Lontra felina", "Lontra canadensis", "Lontra annectens"))) %>% group_by(species1, Species = species) %>% summarise(n = n()) %>% ggplot(aes(x = species1, y = n, fill = Species)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity") + scale_fill_manual(values = c("red", "gray", "blue", "green", "orange", "purple", "darkred")) + theme_light() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) + labs(x = "") ggsave("./output/mink_detection_species_barplot_lontra_spp.png", width = 1200, height = 800, scale = 1.2, units = "px") # ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ # training data: detections actually used after the YOLO-label # step below counts <- read.csv("./data/processed/mink_detection_class_detection_counts.csv") counts %>% mutate(Species = case_when(class_name == "Neogale_vison" ~ "Neogale vison", class_name == "Rattus_rattus" ~ "Rattus rattus", class_name == "Lontra" ~ "Lontra spp.")) %>% rename(n = detection_count) %>% ggplot(aes(x = Species, y = n)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity") + theme_light() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) ggsave("./output/mink_detection_training_data_barplot.png", width = 1200, height = 800, scale = 1.2, units = "px") ``` ::: # Preview pretrained-model detections * Before training a dedicated model, a pretrained YOLO model (trained on COCO classes) is run on a sample of the downloaded images to check whether any COCO class already picks up the focal individuals (the manuscript reports this for the `bird`, `dog`, `cat`, and `bear` classes across YOLO v8, v10, and 26). ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} import cv2 from pathlib import Path from ultralytics import YOLO import time # Paths (relative to the project root) IMAGE_DIR = Path("./data/raw/mink_detection_images") OUTPUT_DIR = Path("./output/mink_detection_test_inference") # Pretrained YOLO model MODEL_NAME = "yolov8l.pt" OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) def main(): start = time.perf_counter() print(f"Loading pretrained YOLO model: {MODEL_NAME}") model = YOLO(MODEL_NAME) image_extensions = {".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".bmp", ".gif", ".webp"} image_files = [f for f in IMAGE_DIR.iterdir() if f.is_file() and f.suffix.lower() in image_extensions] print(f"Found {len(image_files)} images to process") for idx, image_path in enumerate(image_files, 1): print(f"[{idx}/{len(image_files)}] Processing: {image_path.name}") try: results = model(str(image_path), conf=0.5) annotated_frame = results[0].plot() output_path = OUTPUT_DIR / image_path.name cv2.imwrite(str(output_path), annotated_frame) except Exception as e: print(f"Error processing {image_path.name}: {e}") continue print(f"\nInference complete! Labeled images saved to: {OUTPUT_DIR}") print(f"Total images processed: {len(image_files)}") elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start print(f"Runtime: {elapsed:.2f} seconds") if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` ::: # Auto-generate YOLO training labels * Detections from the pretrained model are kept only for the COCO classes that approximate the focal species (`bird`, `dog`, `cat`, `bear`) and remapped to the three focal classes used for training: `0` = American Mink (`Neogale_vison`), `1` = Black Rat (`Rattus_rattus`), `2` = *Lontra* spp. (all `Lontra_*` species pooled). A label file is written only when at least one valid detection survives this filter, which is why a large fraction of the downloaded images end up unused for training (see manuscript for exact counts). ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} from pathlib import Path from ultralytics import YOLO import argparse import time # Paths (relative to the project root) IMAGE_DIR = Path("./data/raw/mink_detection_images") LABEL_DIR = Path("./data/processed/mink_detection_labels") # Pretrained model MODEL_NAME = "yolov8l.pt" # Allowed detector classes from COCO ALLOWED_DETECTION_CLASSES = {"bird", "dog", "cat", "bear"} # Species-to-output-class mapping from filename prefix SPECIES_TO_TARGET_CLASS = { "Neogale_vison": 0, "Rattus_rattus": 1, "Lontra_provocax": 2, "Lontra_annectens": 2, "Lontra_longicaudis": 2, "Lontra_canadensis": 2, "Lontra_felina": 2, } IMAGE_EXTENSIONS = {".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".bmp", ".gif", ".webp"} def parse_args(): parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Run YOLO inference and export filtered YOLO labels.") parser.add_argument( "--limit", type=int, default=None, help="Optional integer limit for number of images to process. If omitted, all images are used." ) parser.add_argument( "--conf", type=float, default=0.5, help="Confidence threshold for YOLO inference." ) return parser.parse_args() def get_species_from_filename(image_path): """Expected filename format: species-id.extension, e.g. Rattus_rattus-INAT383396732.jpeg""" species = image_path.stem.split("-", 1)[0] return species if species in SPECIES_TO_TARGET_CLASS else None def main(): args = parse_args() start = time.perf_counter() LABEL_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) print(f"Loading pretrained YOLO model: {MODEL_NAME}") model = YOLO(MODEL_NAME) model_name_to_id = {name: idx for idx, name in model.names.items()} valid_model_class_ids = { model_name_to_id[name] for name in ALLOWED_DETECTION_CLASSES if name in model_name_to_id } print(f"Detector classes used: {sorted(ALLOWED_DETECTION_CLASSES)}") print(f"Resolved detector class ids: {sorted(valid_model_class_ids)}") image_files = sorted( f for f in IMAGE_DIR.iterdir() if f.is_file() and f.suffix.lower() in IMAGE_EXTENSIONS ) if args.limit is not None: if args.limit < 1: raise ValueError("--limit must be a positive integer") image_files = image_files[:args.limit] print(f"Found {len(image_files)} images to process") processed = 0 exported = 0 skipped_unknown_species = 0 no_valid_detection = 0 for idx, image_path in enumerate(image_files, 1): print(f"[{idx}/{len(image_files)}] Processing: {image_path.name}") species = get_species_from_filename(image_path) if species is None: print(" Skipped: unknown species prefix in filename") skipped_unknown_species += 1 continue target_class = SPECIES_TO_TARGET_CLASS[species] try: results = model.predict(source=str(image_path), conf=args.conf, verbose=False) result = results[0] boxes = result.boxes output_lines = [] if boxes is not None and len(boxes) > 0: cls_list = boxes.cls.tolist() xywhn_list = boxes.xywhn.tolist() for cls_id, xywhn in zip(cls_list, xywhn_list): cls_id = int(cls_id) if cls_id not in valid_model_class_ids: continue x_center, y_center, width, height = xywhn output_lines.append( f"{target_class} {x_center:.6f} {y_center:.6f} {width:.6f} {height:.6f}" ) if output_lines: label_path = LABEL_DIR / f"{image_path.stem}.txt" with open(label_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write("\n".join(output_lines) + "\n") exported += 1 print(f" Exported: {label_path.name} ({len(output_lines)} labels)") else: no_valid_detection += 1 print(" No valid detections (bird/dog/cat/bear), no label exported") processed += 1 except Exception as e: print(f" Error processing {image_path.name}: {e}") continue elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start print("\nInference complete") print(f"Images considered: {len(image_files)}") print(f"Images processed: {processed}") print(f"Label files exported: {exported}") print(f"Skipped due to unknown species prefix: {skipped_unknown_species}") print(f"Images with no valid detections: {no_valid_detection}") print(f"YOLO labels saved to: {LABEL_DIR}") print(f"Runtime: {elapsed:.2f} seconds") if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` ::: # Train / validation split * Images with an exported label are randomly split 80/20 into training and validation sets (fixed seed for reproducibility), and copied into the layout YOLO expects. ::: {.cell} ```{.python .cell-code} from pathlib import Path import random import shutil src_labels = Path("./data/processed/mink_detection_labels") src_images = Path("./data/raw/mink_detection_images") dst_root = Path("./data/processed/mink_detection_yolo_split") train_ratio = 0.8 seed = 42 image_exts = [".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".bmp", ".tif", ".tiff", ".webp"] def find_image(stem): for ext in image_exts: candidate = src_images / f"{stem}{ext}" if candidate.exists(): return candidate matches = [] for ext in image_exts: matches.extend(src_images.glob(f"**/{stem}{ext}")) return matches[0] if matches else None def main(): if not src_labels.exists(): raise FileNotFoundError(f"Labels folder not found: {src_labels}") if not src_images.exists(): raise FileNotFoundError(f"Images folder not found: {src_images}") label_files = sorted(src_labels.glob("*.txt")) pairs = [] missing = [] for label_path in label_files: image_path = find_image(label_path.stem) if image_path is None: missing.append(label_path.name) continue pairs.append((label_path, image_path)) if not pairs: raise RuntimeError("No label-image pairs found.") random.seed(seed) random.shuffle(pairs) split_idx = int(len(pairs) * train_ratio) train_pairs = pairs[:split_idx] val_pairs = pairs[split_idx:] for split_name, split_pairs in [("train", train_pairs), ("val", val_pairs)]: (dst_root / "labels" / split_name).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) (dst_root / "images" / split_name).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) for label_path, image_path in split_pairs: shutil.copy2(label_path, dst_root / "labels" / split_name / label_path.name) shutil.copy2(image_path, dst_root / "images" / split_name / image_path.name) print(f"Total pairs: {len(pairs)}") print(f"Train: {len(train_pairs)}") print(f"Val: {len(val_pairs)}") if missing: print(f"Missing images for {len(missing)} labels:") for name in missing[:20]: print(f" {name}") if len(missing) > 20: print(" ...") if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` ::: # Dataset configuration * YOLO's training command (next section) points at a small YAML file declaring the three focal classes and the train/validation image directories produced above: [`scripts/mink_detection_data.yaml`](mink_detection_data.yaml). ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` names: 0: N_vison 1: R_rattus 2: Lontra_spp nc: 3 train: ./data/processed/mink_detection_yolo_split/images/train val: ./data/processed/mink_detection_yolo_split/images/val ``` ::: ::: # Train the YOLO model * The YOLO v10 nano model is trained from the split above. This step needs a CUDA-capable GPU and was not re-run as part of knitting this document; see the manuscript for the training hardware, runtime, and resulting accuracy metrics (confusion matrix, mAP50, precision). ::: {.cell} ```{.bash .cell-code} yolo detect train data=./scripts/mink_detection_data.yaml model=yolov10l.pt epochs=100 imgsz=640 batch=16 ``` ::: --- # References {.unnumbered .unlisted} - Redmon, J., Divvala, S., Girshick, R., & Farhadi, A. (2016). You only look once: Unified, real-time object detection. *CVPR*. - Jocher, G., Qiu, J., & Chaurasia, A. (2023). Ultralytics YOLO (Version 8.0.0) [Computer software]. https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics # Session information {.unnumbered .unlisted}
